summary: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Khenpo Shenga, and taught numerous prominent students, including Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Calcutta (1959–1965), he held posts at Calcutta, the University of Delhi (1977–1990), and the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).
Dilli Raman Regmi was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed an M.A. at Patna University by around 1944 and earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras.

Dina Bangdel specialized in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University from around 1999 to 2002 and at Virginia Commonwealth University from around 2002 to 2017.

Dines Andersen worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (1879–1892) under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, later serving there as professor of Indian philology (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He became Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta in 1937, succeeding Hemchandra Raychaudhuri, and served as Government Epigraphist for India from around 1949 to 1961.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1993 and became a professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.
Dipak Kumar Barua works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from around 1996 to 1999.

Dipak Ranjan Das works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Dineschandra Sircar and held a post at the University of Calcutta in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture.

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian who studied at the University of Calcutta, IIM Calcutta, and Australian National University. He held posts at the University of Melbourne (~1985–1995) and joined the University of Chicago in 1995.
Dirk H. A. Kolff is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his MA at Leiden University (~1957–1967) and served there as Professor of Modern Indian History from 1967 to 2003.

Diwakar Acharya works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. After earning his PhD at the University of Hamburg (2000–2004), he held positions at Hamburg, Kyoto University (2006–2016), and the University of Oxford (~2016), succeeding Alexis Sanderson.
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from around 1886 to 1889. He later served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dominic Goodall works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and also studied under S. A. Srinivasan, later holding posts at EFEO (2000–2016) and EPHE (2005).

Dominic Sur specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen C. Lang, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and took up a post at Utah State University around 2017.

Dominik Wujastyk works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of London and University of Oxford, later holding posts at the Wellcome Institute, UCL, the University of Vienna, and the University of Alberta (2015).

Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology between 1979 and 1984. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1988.
Dominique-Sila Khan worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University from around 1985 to 1993 and served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies.

Don A. Pittman specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa from around 1980 to 1987, and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University from around 1987 to 2002.

Don Handelman is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at McGill, Pittsburgh, and Manchester universities before serving as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from around 1972 to 2009.
